idiom_name: ROM relations + mappers over plain structs (vs ActiveRecord)
implementation_notes: Ruby's lightweight-entity route is ROM (rom-rb): relations and schemas describe storage, mappers and changesets translate rows into plain structs (dry-struct based) and back, and repositories are the public interface - the domain object itself has no find/save/destroy. That mapper layer replaces ActiveRecord's model classes, which mix persistence into the domain object and are the heavyweight counterexample. A hand-written Sequel dataset plus Struct/Data.define is the simpler replacement for a single table where a full container is not wanted.
code_sketch:
class User < Dry::Struct
  attribute :id, Types::Integer
  attribute :email, Types::String
end

# ROM container: relation + mapper + repository live outside the struct
rom = ROM.container(:sql, 'sqlite::memory') do |c|
  c.relation(:users) { schema(infer: true) { attribute :email, alias: :email_address } }
end
# repo.users.by_id(1) -> User instance; User itself has no persistence API
pitfalls: The dominant Rails stack pushes ActiveRecord, whose models mix persistence into the entity; keeping entities dumb is a boundary decision across the app, not a per-class one.
ROM/Sequel schema blocks and structs are two declarations of one shape and drift unless schema inference or mapping checks are used.
Struct entities are value-like: with in-place mutation or changeset misuse, writes are silently lost unless you go through the repository/changeset API.
